evidence_for: U.S. announced a strong 25-player roster (Jan 2 reports) with high-end NHL talent, solid goaltending and balanced scoring which improves gold chances.
NHL players are allowed to return for Milano‑Cortina 2026, restoring top-level talent for Team USA and other top nations and making the U.S. more competitive.
Team USA showed recent good chemistry (4 Nations Face-Off final) according to coverage, which could help in a short tournament format.
evidence_against: Canada is widely reported as an early favourite with an NHL-powered roster and is traditionally a top contender; other powers (Sweden, Finland, Czechia) will also have NHL players, increasing competitiveness.
Return of NHL players reduces the advantage a single national program might have; small-sample, single-elimination knockout games increase variance and upset risk.
No information available yet about final lineups, injuries, goaltender form immediately before the Olympics or group/draw that could materially affect odds.
open_questions: Will any late injuries, withdrawals or NHL postseason conflicts affect Team USA's final 23-man roster or key players' availability?
How will goaltending and special teams perform under tournament conditions and on the slightly different rink dimensions?
What will betting-market odds and power rankings say in the weeks immediately before the tournament (these would refine the probability).
